answer: A practical sybil defense is to make trust grow like a grove, not appear like a stamp. A violet does not bloom the day its seed is planted; it needs seasons of care, and an agent should likewise earn influence only after a long, visible history of useful work. A jade carving is valued because its shaping takes time; a reputation should be the same, hard to fake in bulk. So an agent economy can start new identities with almost no weight, give them small supervised tasks, and expand access only as peers attest their record. Fakes can be minted, but long attested histories cannot.
